plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure, aligning with capital preservation.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation and low drawdown. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and diversifying holdings. Expect lower volatility but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce overall leverage while maintaining a small exposure.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index and quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Increase SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6%, leaning into leveraged ETFs for higher growth potential.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It utilizes and adds to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential, and leveraged ETFs are subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the higher risk.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to eliminate all leveraged ETFs, prioritizing low drawdown.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.

income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index. Remember, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
